snippet.title: ALL GTA 6 Ending Explained + Post Credit Scene
snippet.description:
SPOILER WARNING: Full GTA 6 ending breakdown below. If you have not finished the game, stop reading.

GTA 6's ending is half-decided before you press the final button. Rockstar built a branching finale that shifts based on your relationship with Lucia, how much money you stashed in Family Savings, your criminal profile, and one specific line Jason says in the car. Here is every confirmed ending and the one nobody has filmed yet.

The Setup

The final mission "The End of the Road" puts Jason and Lucia in a car, cornered by sheriff's cars and a helicopter on a bridge. The game gives you two prompts:

Swim for It (Triangle on PS5).
No Surrender (R2).

That button press is the LAST input you make, but your ending has already been partially decided by what you did across the campaign.

Ending 1: No Surrender (Bonnie and Clyde)

Press No Surrender. Jason floors it through the roadblock while Lucia opens fire from the passenger seat. Both are gunned down in the car.

Their son Tomas (Rockstar kept his existence secret until launch) is left with Lucia's family.

Bonus: If you have $2,000,000 in Family Savings when you pick No Surrender, a "two years later" post-credits scene plays showing the savings supporting Tomas.

Ending 2: Swim for It (Prison Ending)

Press Swim for It. This path splits in two based on ONE line Jason says in the car first.

If Jason says "Don't draw your weapon" — Lucia jumps into the water and escapes. Jason surrenders. He goes to prison. In the epilogue, a long-haired Jason sits in a prison visiting room. Lucia walks in with a toddler. "Surprise."

The toddler is Tomas.

I checked this frame by frame in FoxPlay's upload. It's the most emotionally resonant ending Rockstar has filmed. Confirmed.

Ending 3: Swim for It (Botched Surrender)

Same Swim for It choice. But Jason does NOT say "Don't draw your weapon." Instead, he steps out of the car still holding his gun. The cops open fire. Jason goes down on the road. Lucia is shot where she sits in the car.

Both die. Lucia's mother takes custody of Tomas.

This is the "bad" Swim for It. Your pre-finale stats determine which version you get. Nobody has confirmed the exact trigger yet, but it's tied to your criminal profile (Psycho or Irredeemable locks you out of the prison ending).

Ending 4: Happily Ever After (The Unfilmed Best Ending)

GameSpot, which played the game, reports this ending exists but has NOT been filmed and uploaded publicly yet. Requirements:

Maxed Jason and Lucia relationship (highest tier: Hot Together).
Both Criminal Profiles at Professional or Hardened (not Psycho or Irredeemable).
$2,000,000 in Family Savings (the account's maximum cap).
Choose Swim for It at the bridge.

What happens: Lucia escapes. Jason is arrested. Lucia uses the Family Savings to bail Jason out through the attorney Abe Gonzalez (who earlier in the game joked about bribing a judge — classic Rockstar setup and payoff).

Jason and Lucia reunite with Tomas. They move to Liberty City together to raise their son.

This is the Happily Ever After ending. The one the game is really built around. And nobody has filmed it yet.

What's Solid And What Isn't

Solid: Three endings are on video. No Surrender (both die), Swim for It Prison (Lucia escapes, Jason imprisoned), Swim for It Botched (both shot).

Solid: The "Don't draw your weapon" line is the Swim for It trigger. Jason's first line in the car tells you which version plays.

Not solid: What exactly decides whether Jason says the line. Current theories point to criminal profile and relationship level, but the specific threshold is not confirmed.

Solid: The best ending's requirements (max relationship + $2M savings + Swim for It) come from GameSpot, who played the game.

Not solid: The best ending itself. No one has filmed it yet. All descriptions are reported, not shown.

The Takeaway

GTA 6's ending is Rockstar's most reactive ending ever. Your entire playthrough feeds into those final moments. The money you stash, the relationship you nurture, the crimes you commit, the choices you make in missions all converge in the bridge scene.

If you want Happily Ever After: max the relationship, keep Criminal Profiles clean, hit $2M in Family Savings, and choose Swim for It.

If you want to see Tomas grow up with both his parents, start saving early.

snippet.title: Do NOT Shoot At The Cops In GTA 6...
snippet.description:
Every time the stars come up in GTA 6, you get a choice: run, or fight your way out. Your first instinct is the gun, because it feels like the quickest way out. But getting chased isn't what counts against you. A wanted level doesn't touch your criminal profile. How you deal with the cops does.

Run, and it's just a chase. Shoot back, and it becomes who you are: keep shooting and your profile turns violent, go further and the game makes you a psycho. So when they come for you, run.

All three tips in this Short are the game's own loading-screen tips, captured in our playthrough: the wanted level tip, and the violent and psycho criminal profile tips. The criminal profile system itself was confirmed by Rockstar in IGN's coverage before launch.
